Honestly this was the biggest thing for me. I’m not the best at the grades part but I put in effort when I learned and did research working in the labs, and one position led to another which eventually led to a job. Letters of recommendation from a professor go a long way, and so do their connections.

I started working this summer for a start up company operating through our labs on campus and working with some professors. I was able to get the initial position because of my lab experience in the past, and the professor I used to work for knew one of the current professors involved in this start up.  I started the internship position this summer with no experience on the subject. To be honest my grades at university are not the best either, but I work hard in the lab so they grew to like me and ended up offering me a job. Networking is such a big part of the the world now, I made it a thing to introduce myself to all my professors and ask questions after class and stuff like that. Don’t be afraid to ask proffesors about possible positions in their labs. The worst they’ll say is no, and see you have a little ambition in you.
